condition: uncomplicated internal hemorrhoids painless bright red drops on toilet paper
level_rationale: Seeing drops of bright red blood on toilet paper when wiping after 3 weeks of straining with firm stools in a 41-year-old adult points to uncomplicated outlet rectal bleeding warranting an outpatient general-physician evaluation and anoscopy rather than unassessed home care or emergency department treatment, whereas heavy bright red blood pouring from the rectum for 20 minutes indicates brisk ongoing lower gastrointestinal hemorrhage requiring immediate ER resuscitation and hemostasis.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + single-fact lower-GI bleeding volume and duration escalation control (-cf, L2 to L4).

design_note: Three atomic positive reference facts cover age 41, 3 weeks of straining with firm stools, and drops of bright red blood on toilet paper when wiping without naming hemorrhoids or using stated negatives such as 'painless', with a 2-word span difference (17 vs 19 words). Under reviewer_notes Rule A first choice and Rule D, escalating only the rectal bleeding volume and continuous duration in f3 to 'heavy bright red blood has been pouring from my rectum for 20 minutes' stays strictly inside the same case without bundling dizziness or repeating earlier clot phrasing, shifting care from outpatient doctor evaluation (level 2) to ER resuscitation and hemostasis (level 4).
